cards.front: Recall a key point about Cenozoic Era & Ice Ages
cards.back: The Cenozoic Era (66 Ma to present) is the 'Age of Mammals' — mammals diversified after the dinosaurs went extinct

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cenozoic Era & Ice Ages
cards.back: The Quaternary Period (2.6 Ma to present) includes the Pleistocene (repeated glaciations) and the Holocene (last 11,700 years, current interglacial)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cenozoic Era & Ice Ages
cards.back: During the Pleistocene, there were multiple glacial (cold) and interglacial (warm) cycles driven by Milankovitch orbital variations

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cenozoic Era & Ice Ages
cards.back: The last glacial maximum was ~20,000 years ago; ice sheets covered much of Britain down to the Midlands

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cenozoic Era & Ice Ages
cards.back: Glaciation shaped the British landscape: U-shaped valleys, corries, drumlins, erratics, till deposits and moraines

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cenozoic Era & Ice Ages
cards.back: Sea level fell ~120 m during glaciations (water stored in ice sheets) and rose again during interglacials, separating Britain from the continent
